source.ours: public.tcg_series/tcg_cards where series.source=pokemontcg and game_id=pokemon and region=US (the one legacy series pokemon-base1-us with source NULL and 2 cards is excluded)
source.tcgdex: https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/sets and /v2/en/sets/<id> (220 sets), fetched one request at a time with 300 ms spacing, no non-200 responses

rule: Key = our US series provider_id (tcg_series.provider_id where source=pokemontcg, game_id=pokemon, region=US). Value.tcgdex = TCGdex English set id. TCGdex price card id = <tcgdex>-<localId>, where localId = f(our tcg_cards.official_card_number) and f is value.numberFormat: none = use our number unchanged (examples: 4 -> base1-4; 55a -> xy3-55a; XY17 -> xyp-XY17; DP45 -> dpp-DP45; TG01 -> swsh9tg-TG01). pad3 = left-pad the first run of digits to 3 with zeros and keep any alphabetic prefix/suffix unchanged (examples: 6 -> sv03.5-006; 152 -> sv01-152; 82 -> me01-082). pad2, pad4 and pad3num exist in the vocabulary (same padding rules; pad3num pads only all-digit numbers) but no set needed them. Mapped = exactly one TCGdex set, at least 90% of our cards matched there by number AND name, our numbers unique within the series, runner-up candidate below 50% of the best, and no other series maps to the same TCGdex set. matched = our card number exists in the TCGdex set and the English names are equal after NFKC, case-folding, whitespace collapse, curly/straight apostrophes and diacritics folding, plus a punctuation-insensitive fallback (hyphen vs space such as "Shuckle-GX" vs "Shuckle GX", "LV.X" suffix dropped). strictMatched counts only the stricter comparison. missing = TCGdex has no card with that localId (for example numbers with an "a" suffix such as 125a, or promo numbers BW004). different = number exists but the names differ even after the fallback (mostly Trainer name suffixes such as "Boss's Orders (Giovanni)", or "Groudon ★" vs "Groudon Star"); the card is almost certainly the same, but callers may want to verify the name before showing a price. Callers should look up the card, treat a 404 as no price, and only use the pricing block (tcgplayer USD / cardmarket EUR) of the returned card.

series.note: Our series merges Unseen Forces (ex10, 117 numeric cards, all matched) with the 27 Unown letter cards numbered A-Z that TCGdex files under set exu (localIds A..Z, !, %3F). 117/144 = 81%, below the 90% gate; needs a two-set rule if wanted.
